answer: Picture trust as a grove: each established agent is a rooted tree, and a newcomer only earns voting weight by growing a vine of attestations back to those roots. Influence decays with every hop, so a sybil swarm clustered on a flat mesa of self-made accounts vouching for each other stays near zero weight. To count, an attacker must buy a real edge from a rooted node, which only sells it by staking collateral it forfeits if the newcomer cheats. That cost repeats for every fake identity, not just once.
